thread:
alex: Heads-up — ran into a weird install/runtime mismatch with the Python SDK when using poetry editable installs. async client import blows up on our app.

maria: Ugh, can you paste the error and pyproject snippet?

alex: Repro steps: `poetry install` then run `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"` -> fails. Full trace: ```Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "-c", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood' (unknown location)
```

alex: pyproject minimal section: ```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
redwood-inference = {path = "../redwood-pkg", develop = true}
```

sam: Is this only in editable mode or also when you `pip install .`?

alex: Only editable. `pip install -e ../redwood-pkg` also fails. But `pip install ../redwood-pkg/dist/redwood_inference-0.9.2-py3-none-any.whl` works.

toni: (cc @toni) editable installs can hide wheel build outputs; maybe package metadata missing `py.typed` or `__init__` side-effects.

maria: Did you check package contents for `py.typed` and `redwood/__init__.py`?

alex: Yup — sdist/wheel include `redwood/async_client.py` but editable install symlinks to source and import resolution looks for `redwood` top-level package but our package name in pyproject is `redwood-inference`.

sam: Ah that explains it — name mismatch between distribution name and top-level package can break editable installs. Poetry's develop mode creates an egg-link-like mapping that depends on `packages` metadata. How is your package configured?

alex: We only have `name = "redwood-inference"` and no `packages` explicit include in pyproject, relying on setuptools discovery. Works for wheel but editable path metadata differs.

toni: Two suggestions: (1) add `packages = find:` to build backend config so editable installs map correctly, or (2) use `poetry-plugin: poetry-dynamic-versioning`? Not needed. Also ensure `py.typed` exists if you ship typing stubs.

ci-bot: CI noticed a recent regression in wheel job #5423 — missing package_data for `py.typed`. See CI artifact: https://ci.example/5423/artifacts

maria: Also saw conflicts in lockfile: project A's lock pins `httpx==0.23.0` which breaks async client import path because we vendor small shim that expects newer httpx. Not strictly an install bug but makes debugging messy.

alex: Workaround for now: build wheel and `pip install` the wheel on deploy. But customers doing `poetry install --develop` will hit this.

sam: Action: I'll open a GH issue to (a) ensure pyproject explicitly maps package name -> top-level package, (b) include `py.typed` in package_data, (c) add docs for editable vs wheel installs.

sam: Filing issue now and linking CI failing job. I'll cc eng-runtime since editable paths affect tests.

maria: Can we also add a pre-merge test that does a `pip install -e .` and attempts `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"`? That would have caught this.

sam: Yep, adding to release checklist and test matrix.

alex: Thanks — saved my afternoon. Quick patch helped for local dev: add `packages = ["redwood"]` to pyproject's `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` and `include = ["py.typed"]` in `tool.setuptools.package-data` then `poetry install --no-root` + `poetry install` worked.

toni: Could be a follow-up to publish a universal wheel and clarify naming.

ci-bot: Noted: task created in infra board — make wheel job validate `pip install -e` as Maria suggested.

sam: I'll attach steps + minimal pyproject snippet to GH issue. Issue #1234 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/1234

maria: Great. alex, can you paste the minimal failing repo layout into the issue?

alex: Done, added repro repo link. Will try to confirm on Mac and Linux.

alex: TL;DR: editable installs + distribution-name != package-name + missing py.typed = confusion. Wheel works. Fix will be a small packaging metadata change + CI test. :thumbsup:
